learningObjectives: Define a mail server connection and explain when the connection is actually established.
Send and reply to email from a TestCase using the Send Mail Module.
Choose correctly between Receive Mail Simple and Receive Mail Expert.
Distinguish engine-level protocol support from current receive Module restrictions and cloud authentication.
Check provider/account prerequisites and keep independently configured SMTP and IMAP connections uniquely named.

elements.term: Mail as part of the business process
elements.description: Very few end-to-end processes finish inside the application. Register an account and a confirmation email arrives; place an order and an order confirmation follows; reset a password and the whole flow depends on a link that only exists in an inbox. If the test stops at the web page, the part the customer actually receives goes untested.
Mail Engine 3.0 is part of the standard Tosca installation. Current Standard subset location: Standard modules → Engines → Mail.

elements.title: Connection, sending and receiving Modules
items: Connect to Mail Server — defines a generic mail server connection.
Connect to Exchange Server — a dedicated Module for Microsoft Exchange connections.
Send Mail — sends or replies to a message via SMTP.
Receive Mail Simple — checks for one specific, single email.
Receive Mail Expert — checks for specific emails with richer matching criteria.
Connect to Cloud Mail Server — OAuth integrations for Microsoft Office 365 and Google Workspace.

bulletPoints: Mail Engine 3.0 ships with standard Tosca; its Modules live in the Standard subset.

elements.description: Connect to Mail Server defines a named server configuration. Network use occurs during sending or receiving, so this configuration step alone does not prove delivery or retrieval.

Connect to Exchange Server configures an EWS endpoint. Current Authentication Type values are Basic (legacy) and OAuth, selected with ActionMode Select. OAuth uses App Id and Tenant Id from a Microsoft identity registration; token-acquisition failure can fail this step, unlike the legacy configuration path.

Connect to Cloud Mail Server has a separate Microsoft Office 365 integration with Tenant Id, Application Id, Client Secret and Mailbox. Its documented prerequisites include a registered Entra application and Graph mail permissions. Google Workspace uses a service-account JSON key and domain-wide delegation. These integrations are not interchangeable with a generic SMTP server or a personal Gmail login.

elements.text: Use the integration supported by your installed Tosca version and the tenant’s approved authentication configuration. Exchange Online EWS disablement starts in October 2026 and completes in April 2027; an EWS OAuth token does not guarantee continued endpoint availability. Check current provider guidance before running an exercise.

elements.title: Supported protocols
items: Engine overview lists SMTP, IMAP, POP3 and EWS.
The 2026.1 Receive Mail Simple and Receive Mail Expert reference explicitly limits these Modules to POP3 or IMAP; do not generalize the overview to each Module.
Cloud integration prerequisites and provider restrictions require a separate check.

bulletPoints: Configuration does not prove mail delivery; OAuth token acquisition can itself fail.
Current receive Module reference: POP3 or IMAP. The engine overview also lists EWS.
Cloud, Exchange EWS and generic mail server connections have different authentication fields.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Real-world setup notes: Gmail and corporate mailboxes

elements.text: An EWS endpoint is not a Gmail IMAP or SMTP endpoint. Select the provider-compatible connection Module rather than substituting a Gmail address in Exchange Web Services Url.

elements.description: Google documents imap.gmail.com:993 with SSL and smtp.gmail.com:587 with TLS (or 465 with SSL). Configure receiving and sending separately with their corresponding protocols and security enabled; successful use still depends on account policy and supported authentication.

elements.title: Personal Gmail prerequisites
items: Google recommends Sign in with Google where supported. If a client lacks it, an app password may be available after enabling 2-Step Verification.
App passwords may be unavailable for organization accounts, Advanced Protection or security-key-only verification; enabling 2-Step Verification alone does not guarantee availability.
Personal Gmail IMAP is always enabled since January 2025. Managed Workspace restrictions are separate.
Use approved credentials and investigate authentication errors; confirming a security alert is not a guaranteed repair. App passwords are revoked after changing the account password.

elements.text: Use unique Connection Name values for separately configured SMTP and IMAP resources so later steps reference the intended protocol. Do not depend on an undocumented last-definition-wins behavior.

Authentication failures depend on the protocol, tenant and provider. A personal Outlook.com or Gmail account is not a universal bypass. Check approved account access, permissions and the installed Module’s requirements.

bulletPoints: EWS, IMAP and SMTP are distinct endpoint types.
Use unique names for separately configured connections.
App-password availability depends on the account; it is not required for every cloud integration.

elements.description: The Send Mail Module sends — or replies to — an email message via SMTP. Typical uses in a test are triggering an inbound process (a system that acts on incoming mail), or generating a message the test will later verify was received and correctly handled.

bulletPoints: Send Mail covers both new messages and replies.

elements.description: Checks whether you received one specific, single email. This is the right choice for the common case: 'after registering, did the confirmation email arrive?' One expected message, one check.
Receive Mail Expert searches a set of messages and exposes a ResultCount plus individual Mail nodes. Use it when the test needs to assert the number of matches or inspect multiple results.

elements.text: The 2026.1 Module reference states POP3/IMAP for both receive Modules, even though the engine overview also lists EWS. Simple can filter and verify a single message; Expert adds explicit result count and multiple-result handling. Inspect the installed Module and cloud integration guidance for other connections.

📄 Official Tricentis Academy exercise material for this lesson is not redistributed here — complete the exercises inside the official course. This lesson needs a working mail account, so check that prerequisite before starting.

bulletPoints: Simple = one specific message; Expert adds explicit result count and multiple Mail nodes.
Both current receive Module entries state POP3/IMAP; engine-level support is not a Module-level guarantee.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming the Connect step proves the server is reachable
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Seeing the Connect to Mail Server TestStep pass and concluding the mail configuration is correct.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The generic Connect step configures a named connection; send/receive establishes network use. OAuth token acquisition may be validated earlier. Verify the operation needed by the test, not merely the connection configuration.

examPitfalls.title: Reaching for Receive Mail Expert by default
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Using the Expert Module for a straightforward 'did the confirmation email arrive?' check because it sounds more capable.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Receive Mail Simple exists precisely for a single specific email and keeps the TestStep readable. Use Expert when you genuinely need to check multiple emails or more complex matching criteria.

examPitfalls.title: Expecting webmail or arbitrary mail services to work
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Trying to point the receive Modules at a mail service that exposes neither Exchange, POP3, nor IMAP.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use the protocols and integration supported by the actual Module. Current Simple/Expert entries specify POP3/IMAP; the engine overview also lists EWS. A webmail interface is not itself a supported mail server endpoint.

examPitfalls.title: Treating Microsoft cloud and EWS configurations as equivalent
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Configuring a standard SMTP connection with username and password for a Microsoft-hosted mailbox.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use the documented integration and tenant-approved credentials. Cloud Office 365 uses Entra application fields and Graph permissions; Exchange EWS has its own OAuth configuration and endpoint lifecycle. Do not claim all SMTP basic authentication is universally unavailable from an old course note.

examPitfalls.title: Reusing one Connection Name for both SMTP and IMAP
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Configuring one Connect to Mail Server step for IMAP and another for SMTP against the same mailbox, but giving both steps the same Connection Name.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Give independently configured SMTP and IMAP resources unique names, then reference the intended name in send/receive. Do not rely on undocumented replacement behavior.

examPitfalls.title: Pointing Connect to Exchange Server at a non-Exchange mailbox
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Entering a Gmail (or other non-Microsoft) address and password into Connect to Exchange Server's Exchange Web Services Url field, expecting it to connect.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use the Gmail-compatible IMAP/SMTP settings or the documented Workspace cloud integration where applicable; an EWS Url is not a Gmail mail-server address.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A TestCase must verify that a single order-confirmation email arrived after checkout. Which Module is the appropriate choice?
practiceQuiz.hint: One specific, single email is expected.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Receive Mail Simple checks whether one specific, single email was received — exactly this scenario. Receive Mail Expert is for checking multiple emails or more complex matching criteria.

optionExplanations.A: This creates or replies to a message rather than checking receipt.
optionExplanations.B: This is the intended Module for verifying one specific received message.
optionExplanations.C: Expert can handle results, but is unnecessary for the stated single-message check.
optionExplanations.D: This configures an OAuth integration; it is not the receipt assertion.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which protocols are explicitly listed for Receive Mail Simple and Receive Mail Expert in the Tosca 2026.1 Module reference?

options.text: Any protocol the mail server exposes

practiceQuiz.hint: Use the specific Module reference, not the broader engine overview.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The specific receive Module entries list POP3 and IMAP. The broader engine overview also lists EWS; that does not establish EWS support for every receive Module.

optionExplanations.A: SMTP is used for sending rather than these receive Module entries.
optionExplanations.B: Both specific 2026.1 receive Module entries state POP3 or IMAP.
optionExplanations.C: Support is bounded by the Module and integration, not arbitrary provider protocols.
optionExplanations.D: A browser webmail interface is not the receive Modules’ POP3/IMAP server connection.

practiceQuiz.scenario: With the generic Connect to Mail Server Module, when does the actual server connection occur?

options.text: As soon as the Connect to Mail Server TestStep executes.
During the sending or receiving step.
When the Tosca workspace is opened.
Only at the end of the ExecutionList.

practiceQuiz.hint: The Connect step defines something; it does not yet do it.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Connect to Mail Server TestStep defines the connection, but the actual connection happens during sending or receiving. A passing Connect step is therefore not proof that the mail server is reachable.

optionExplanations.A: This defines the generic connection configuration, not the sending/receiving operation.
optionExplanations.B: Actual generic server connection occurs when the sending or receiving step uses it.
optionExplanations.C: Opening a workspace does not perform this configured mail operation.
optionExplanations.D: Connections are used when the relevant operation executes, not only at the list’s end.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A test needs the documented Microsoft Office 365 cloud mailbox integration. Which connection Module and prerequisites fit?

options.text: Send Mail with basic authentication — it is simplest.
Connect to Cloud Mail Server, with an Entra application, client secret and required Graph mail permissions.
Receive Mail Expert, because cloud mailboxes are read-only.
Microsoft 365 mailboxes cannot be automated with Tosca.

practiceQuiz.hint: The cloud Office 365 integration has its own Entra application configuration.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The cloud Module documents these prerequisites for Office 365. It does not mean every SMTP scenario accepts the same configuration; choose the integration required by the test.

optionExplanations.A: A sending Module alone does not configure the required cloud OAuth integration.
optionExplanations.B: These are the documented Office 365 cloud integration prerequisites.
optionExplanations.C: A receive assertion does not create the connection; cloud mailboxes are not inherently read-only.
optionExplanations.D: The cloud Module documents Office 365 integration, subject to prerequisites and permissions.

quickRecap.value: Standard installation; current Modules under Standard modules → Engines → Mail.
Defines the connection — the connection itself is made during send/receive.
Cloud Office 365: Entra app, client secret and Graph permissions. EWS OAuth is a different connection; check endpoint lifecycle.
IMAP (receive): imap.gmail.com:993. SMTP (send): smtp.gmail.com:587. Both need Enable Security = True.
App passwords require 2-Step Verification but may be unavailable. Prefer provider-supported sign-in where applicable.
Use unique names for independently configured SMTP and IMAP resources.
EWS endpoints are distinct from Gmail IMAP/SMTP servers.
Sends or replies to a message via SMTP.
Checks for ONE specific, single email.
Multiple-result handling with ResultCount and individual Mail nodes.
Current Simple/Expert reference: POP3 or IMAP. Broader engine overview also lists EWS.
